**Third review round (2026-09-02), 7 of 8 angles.** What it caught and what held:

- **A desired-state guard on an observed event hides the deletion it is supposed
  to catch.** My "ignore an empty userCode report when a PIN is expected" guard,
  stacked on the pre-existing AVAILABLE one, left a User Code CC lock with no path
  at all for an out-of-band deletion — no polls, no drift read. Reverted. Rule:
  suppressing an observation because you *wanted* something else is the #1538
  shape; the pre-existing AVAILABLE guard has the same hole (follow-up).
- **Gate on the property, not the caller.** `source == "sync"` was standing in for
  "is there a tick to expire this entry" — that's `is_slot_managed(slot)`. The
  wrong gate let a direct write to a managed slot leave a lagging sync write
  pending, so the next read confirmed the *old* PIN as truth.
- **Two stores about one write: store what only one side knows, derive the rest.**
  `_unverified` = *believed value pushed optimistically* (only the coordinator
  knows); pending = read off `lock.has_pending_write()`. `is_verified = not believed
  and not pending`. Deriving *everything* from pending was wrong: after an
  optimistic timeout the believed value is still in `data` and must stay untrusted.
- **A debounced refresh is not a read.** Skipping the tick's post-set read because
  "the seam already refreshed" broke same-tick in-sync: the seam's
  `async_request_refresh` was deferred by cooldown. The poller CONFIRMED path now
  does `async_confirm_pending_writes(force=True)` itself, like OPTIMISTIC does.
- **Charge only when a read has had its say.** `coordinator.read_completed_since(
  deadline - TTL)` gates the timeout charge; an outage that outlived the deadline
  is not the lock declining the write.
- **Under freezegun, "before" and "now" are the same instant.** A test that records
  a write right after a read must `freezer.tick(1)` first or `>=` makes them equal.
- **Anchored scripted edits fail loudly when the commit hook's `ruff format` has
  rewrapped the text since you wrote it.** Re-read before re-applying; never assume

## Proposed change

One of the four symptoms in #1538: LCM reported users as **in sync** while `matter.get_lock_users` showed the lock held no PIN credentials at all.

### The bug

The in-sync check would override a lock that said the slot held nothing, on the strength of the last PIN it wrote there:

```python
if credential.is_empty:
    # If we recently set a PIN on this slot and it matches the
    # configured PIN, trust the set — the provider may not
    # have caught up yet (eventual consistency, e.g. Schlage cloud API).
    return (self._last_set_pin is not None
            and snapshot.credential_state == self._last_set_pin)
```

Nothing made it *recent*: `_last_set_pin` was set on every successful write and cleared only by a clear or a restart. A poll that read the slot empty marked the address verified, so the guard above passed, and a credential deleted out of band read as synchronized forever — with no tick to put it back, because a slot in sync is a slot with nothing to do.

### The fix, as it stands after three review rounds

The seam already recorded an **optimistic** write as pending, and `_apply_read` already refused to mark an absent read verified while a write was pending on that address. A **confirmed** write on a polled lock is the same case — "confirmed" there is the cloud accepting it, not the lock reporting it — so it is now recorded pending too, for a managed slot. Then `calculate_in_sync` needs no clock: a verified empty read is the lock's answer, and an active slot the lock says is empty is out of sync, whatever was last written.

Around that core:

- **A write is trusted until a read has seen it, and the tick asks for that read.** While a write is pending the tick calls `async_confirm_pending_writes` on every pass; the coordinator throttles to one read per quarter of the time to live, against its last read of any kind. A polled lock's confirmed write also reads straight back, forced past the throttle, exactly as an optimistic write always has — so when the lock already reports the write, the slot is in sync on the same tick; only a lagging read leaves it pending. The deadline stays at `PENDING_WRITE_TTL` (60 s) and is *not* stretched by the scan interval: three timeouts have to fit inside the slot breaker's five-minute window, or a write the lock never keeps could never trip it.
- **The timeout charges the breaker only when a read has completed since the write.** An outage that outlives the deadline, or reads that keep failing, is not the lock declining the write. Reachability is judged before the pending check, so such an outage suspends the slot as it always did.
- **`is_verified` derives its pending half from the lock's record** rather than mirroring it, so nothing can forget to unmark. The stored `_unverified` set keeps the one thing only the coordinator knows: a believed value an optimistic write pushed, which must stay untrusted after that write times out.
- **Push providers are unchanged in contract**: each pushes the value itself (or the driver's event does) before returning CONFIRMED. zwave_js was the one that did not, and now does.
- **The last PIN written lives on the provider** (`BaseLock.last_set_pin`) beside `last_write_was_clear`, for the reason that docstring already gave: direct service writes bypass the sync manager. Forgotten before any write is sent, since a write that raises may still have landed.

### What each review round changed

| Round | What it found | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A 60 s deadline on the old override was consulted lazily (push-only locks never re-asked), consulted right after arming (breaker reset on every cycle → unbounded rewrite loop; on Schlage that deletes a working code each poll), and was a fourth trust record on the wrong layer. | Replaced the deadline with the pending-write design above (`69cb56b2`, `5c02b3b5`). |
| 2 | Deadline of TTL+interval exceeded the breaker window (never trips on Schlage); a poller's write was pending on the lock but verified on the coordinator; zwave_js returned CONFIRMED without pushing (stale `empty()` → charged for a code the lock held). | TTL-only deadline with active re-reads; `mark_unverified` on record; zwave_js pushes on CONFIRMED (`01bc6993`, `95260f83`). |
| 3 | My new empty-userCode guard, stacked on the older AVAILABLE guard, left a User Code CC lock with **no path** for an out-of-band deletion — #1538 reintroduced on zwave_js. `source == "sync"` was the wrong gate (a direct write to a managed slot left a lagging sync entry standing). `mark_unverified` had made the two stores drift (a disabled slot cleared itself every tick). | Guard reverted; gate on `is_slot_managed`; pending half derived; forced read after a poller's confirmed write; read-gated timeout charge (`2287553a`). |

Two review suggestions declined, with the reasoning in the commit messages: deriving `is_verified` *entirely* from pending (breaks the optimistic-timeout case), and having the seam push `known(pin)` for every push-provider CONFIRMED (would overwrite Matter's deliberate `unreadable()`). Two follow-ups noted, not in this PR: the pre-existing AVAILABLE guard has the same deletion-hiding shape my reverted one had; and the three "expects a PIN" guards across zwave_js/zwave_js_ui should be one predicate or none.

### Known trade

A Schlage cloud whose read lags a write by more than ~60 s despite four confirmation reads will time out, rewrite (delete-then-add), and after three such cycles suspend the slot with a repair. Before this PR that lag was invisible and the slot was green. I have no sourced number for Schlage's actual propagation lag; if it turns out to exceed a minute, `PENDING_WRITE_TTL` is the knob and this is the place that says so.

## Testing

`tests/properties/test_in_sync.py` had encoded the bug as the invariant; it now states the real one, with an explicit *same-as-last-set* axis — two independent random draws almost never collide, so the branch that mattered was untested before.

The tick tests drive the **real coordinator and the real clock** (`freezer`) rather than hand-feeding `_apply_read`; the mock lock's unscoped read now mirrors the base projection (managed slots reported empty rather than omitted), which is what let the pending flow be tested through the real refresh at all.

Mutation-tested each round rather than trusted to coverage. Round 3: nine mutants, nine killed by named tests; removing the forced read alone fails eleven.

Full suite green (2359 passed), coverage gate held, CI green.

## History

This branch briefly carried a fix for the `lcm3`/`lcm4`/`lcm5` name degradation, reverted in `912ba8db` after two review rounds showed it could suppress the fallback cascade in cases where descending was the only way to get a working PIN onto the lock. That symptom is cosmetic, self-healing on the next write, and gets its own change.

Nothing left is independent of your decision, so this is the report.

## Where #1539 stands

**The core fix is right and has been since `69cb56b2`:** a verified empty read on an active slot is out of sync. That's the #1538 bug, and it's fixed on every provider.

**The confirmation machinery around it did not converge in four review rounds**, and the pattern is unambiguous — each round's fix produced a finding of equal weight in the next:

| Round | Introduced |
|---|---|
| 1 | A 60 s trust window: never re-checked on push-only locks; breaker reset on every cycle |
| 2 | Deadline longer than the breaker window (never trips on Schlage); zwave_js never pushed its value |
| 3 | A guard that hid out-of-band deletions; the wrong gate; two stores drifting |
| 4 | One Schlage cloud blip now suspends **every slot on the lock in ~6 s**; throttle stops throttling when reads fail; overlapping ticks queue N reads; push providers with failing reads loop forever uncharged — a regression from `main` |

Two review angles named the cause independently, and I agree with them: **the sync tick and the coordinator are two schedulers negotiating over one lock's reads.** Every fix I made added a coordination *rule* between them instead of giving one of them ownership. That is the smell your heuristic was pointing at, and I went one round past where I should have stopped.

**Actions taken:** PR #1539 is now **draft** — as pushed it is worse than `main` for a Schlage user with a flaky cloud, and it shouldn't look mergeable. The full four-round verdict is a comment on the PR so it isn't lost, and in memory with the meta-lesson.

## The decision that's yours

**Option A — land the narrow fix, defer the machinery.** Reset the branch to `69cb56b2` + `5c02b3b5` (the pending design with a TTL+interval deadline and no active re-reads) plus the trivial comment fixes. Known hole: a write the lock never keeps on Schlage rewrites every ~6 minutes without ever tripping the breaker — annoying, visible in logs, and strictly safer than anything since. It fixes #1538 on Matter and Z-Wave today.

**Option B — the redesign, in this PR or the next.** The coordinator owns pending writes end to end: records them, schedules its own confirmation reads with `async_call_later` at TTL/4, confirms on presence, and expires inside `_apply_read` — the one place a read has by definition completed. The tick becomes an observer of `has_pending_write`. That deletes the `is_slot_managed` gate, `read_completed_since`, the deadline arithmetic, `force=`, and the throttle. It's the design the codebase already half-implies; it's a day of work with a fresh review, not a patch.

**My recommendation is A now, B as its own PR.** The reporter has a security-relevant false in-sync today; the confirmation-scheduling problem is real but pre-dates this branch in shape, and it deserves to be designed rather than iterated into existence under review pressure.

One more thing the fourth round surfaced that's independent of all this: `MockLCMPushLock` returns CONFIRMED without pushing — it's in breach of the exact convention zwave_js was patched to follow, so the fixture that would catch a push provider breaking it can't.

    def _apply_read(
        self, observed: dict[CredentialAddress, SlotCredential]
    ) -> dict[CredentialAddress, SlotCredential]:
        """
        Resolve a genuine read (poll or hard refresh) against pending writes.

        A read is the dropped-push backstop for the verified-credential
        lifecycle: for a slot with an outstanding optimistic write, observing
        the slot present confirms our write -- keep the believed value and mark
        it verified. The one exception (mirroring ``BaseLock._confirm_slot``) is
        a *readable* observation of a different code: that is an external change
        racing our write, so take the observation rather than masking it with
        the believed value -- otherwise a drift refresh, whose whole purpose is
        to surface out-of-band changes, would silently overwrite one. Observing
        the slot still absent means the write has not landed yet, so keep waiting
        (stay unverified, pending intact). Slots with no pending write are
        genuine observations and are marked verified. See the Phase 2
        push-as-commit spec.
        """
        out: dict[CredentialAddress, SlotCredential] = {}
        for address, cred in observed.items():
            pending = self._lock._pending_writes.get(address)
            if pending is not None and cred.is_present:
                pin, _deadline = pending
                del self._lock._pending_writes[address]
                if cred.is_readable and cred.readable_pin != pin:
                    out[address] = cred
                else:
                    out[address] = SlotCredential.known(pin)
                self._unverified.discard(address)
            elif pending is not None:
                out[address] = cred
                self._unverified.add(address)
            else:
                out[address] = cred
                self._unverified.discard(address)
        # Keep the unverified set in lockstep with the read.
        self._unverified &= out.keys()
        return out

        Unlisted addresses are verified: an address is only unverified while

        return _checked(address) not in self._unverified

        optimistic write on the same address cannot strand it.

async def async_confirm_pending_writes(self) -> None:
        """
        Actively read the lock back to confirm outstanding optimistic writes.

        An ambiguous write (``WriteResult.OPTIMISTIC``) gets no confirming push
        on some stacks: node-zwave-js, for one, emits no ``credential
        added/modified`` event when its own post-write verification fails on a
        lock that reports codes back masked -- the event and the ``ERROR_UNKNOWN``
        result are mutually exclusive. Waiting for the hourly drift refresh would
        let the breaker suspend a slot whose code actually landed (~3 attempts in
        the 5-minute window, long before the hourly backstop). So the seam calls
        this immediately after recording an optimistic write.

        This is the order-independent confirmation path: it does not depend on
        receiving any event. A hard read observes the slot present-but-masked
        (LCM projects masked codes to ``unreadable`` rather than repeating the
        driver's ``userCode == codeData`` check) and ``_apply_read`` confirms it;
        a genuinely-absent slot stays pending and re-syncs on the next tick.

        A failed read is non-fatal and does not apply backoff: the slot stays
        pending and the sync tick reconciles it within the TTL.
        """
        if not self._lock._pending_writes:

        try:

                self._normalize_keys(
                    await self._lock.async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()

            # must not escape into the set seam and suspend the slot. The pending

# Pending writes, owned by the coordinator (Option B for #1538)

Local design note; docs/ is gitignored.

## Problem
Four review rounds on #1539 showed the sync tick and the coordinator acting as
two schedulers over one lock's reads. Every fix added a coordination rule
(throttle, force, read stamp, gate-first, read_completed_since, skip-second-read).

## Design
The coordinator owns a write's life from "sent" to "seen":

- `record_write(address, pin, *, believed)` — stores `PendingWrite(pin, written_at,
  believed)`; if believed, sets `data[address]=known(pin)`; arms ONE timer per
  coordinator (`async_call_later`, delay 0 for the first look, then
  `CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL = TTL/4`) if not already armed.
- `_async_confirmation_read` — if nothing pending, disarm. Else read the pending
  addresses plus the managed scope: pollers via `async_internal_get_usercodes(scope)`,
  push providers via `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()`; resolve through
  `_apply_read`; never charges the lock breaker (connectivity is the poll's job).
  A read that FAILS past an entry's deadline expires that entry with the flag.
  Re-arm if anything is still pending.
- `_apply_read` — pending+present → confirm (pop; believed→known(pin), readable
  different→observation). pending+absent past deadline → EXPIRE: pop, take the
  observation, set `expired_unconfirmed` flag. pending+absent before deadline → keep.
- `is_verified(address)` == `address not in _pending`. `_unverified` is deleted:
  a believed value is replaced by the observation on expiry, so nothing stale survives.
- `observe_push(address, observed)` — `_confirm_slot`'s body, on the coordinator.
- `drop_pending(address)` — clear path / stale desired state; no flag.
- `take_expired(address) -> bool` — one-shot; the tick charges the slot breaker.

Tick: no I/O in PENDING. If pending and still wanted → PENDING_CONFIRMATION.
If pending and not wanted → drop, OUT_OF_SYNC. If `take_expired` → record_failure,
warn, OUT_OF_SYNC. Post-set: pending → PENDING_CONFIRMATION; else verify as before.

Seam: OPTIMISTIC → `record_write(believed=True)`; CONFIRMED on push → nothing
pending (provider pushed); CONFIRMED on a poller → `record_write(believed=False)`,
any slot (unmanaged slots get confirmation for free, no is_slot_managed gate).
Clear → `drop_pending`. `_confirm_slot` delegates to `observe_push`.

Carried from #1539: `calculate_in_sync` verified-empty → False (+ property/unit
tests with the same-as-last-set axis); zwave_js pushes known(pin) on CONFIRMED;
mock lock's unscoped read mirrors the projection; `MockLCMPushLock` pushes on set.
NOT carried: `_last_set_pin` move to the provider (Matter release bypass hole).

## Invariants to mutation-test
1. verified-empty active slot is never in sync.
2. a poller's CONFIRMED write is pending until a read sees it; confirmed by presence.
3. expiry happens only inside a completed (or failed-past-deadline) read; the tick
   charges exactly once per expiry.
4. one confirmation timer per coordinator; N pending slots → one read per interval.
5. a stale (desired changed) drop does not charge.
6. push CONFIRMED records nothing; zwave_js pushes before returning.

async def test_sync_tracker_does_not_fire_breaker_with_expired_window(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """
    Test that stale sync attempts outside the window do not trigger the circuit breaker.

    When the attempt window expires, record_failure resets the counter,
    preventing stale counts from triggering the breaker on a new sync cycle.
    """
    await async_initial_tick(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)

    in_sync_entity_obj = get_in_sync_entity_obj(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)
    sync_mgr = in_sync_entity_obj._sync_manager

    # Verify in sync
    assert hass.states.get(SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY).state == STATE_ON

    # Simulate prior sync attempts from an EXPIRED window
    sync_mgr._slot_breaker._failure_count = MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS - 1
    sync_mgr._slot_breaker._first_failure = dt_util.utcnow() - SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW * 2

    # Change PIN to trigger out-of-sync
    await hass.services.async_call(
        TEXT_DOMAIN,
        TEXT_SERVICE_SET_VALUE,
        service_data={ATTR_VALUE: "9999"},
        target={ATTR_ENTITY_ID: SLOT_1_PIN_ENTITY},
        blocking=True,
    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    # _request_sync_check transitions IN_SYNC -> OUT_OF_SYNC
    assert sync_mgr._state is SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC

    # Tick fires — expired window causes record_failure to reset the
    # counter, so the breaker does not fire. Sync succeeds and resets the
    # breaker.
    await sync_mgr._async_tick()
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    # Sync succeeded — lock should be IN_SYNC, not SUSPENDED
    assert sync_mgr._state is SyncState.IN_SYNC
    # Breaker reset after successful sync
    assert sync_mgr._slot_breaker.failure_count == 0


async def test_sync_tracker_expired_window_resets(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """Test that sync attempt tracker resets when the time window expires."""
    lock_provider = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.locks[LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]
    coordinator = lock_provider.coordinator
    assert coordinator is not None

    in_sync_entity_obj = get_in_sync_entity_obj(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)

    # Set up breaker with max attempts but with an expired window
    in_sync_entity_obj._sync_manager._slot_breaker._failure_count = MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS
    in_sync_entity_obj._sync_manager._slot_breaker._first_failure = (
        dt_util.utcnow() - SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW * 2
    )

    # tripped should be False since the breaches fall outside the window
    assert not in_sync_entity_obj._sync_manager._slot_breaker.tripped

async def test_push_update_during_sync_operation_does_not_corrupt_state(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
):
    """
    A coordinator push_update during _perform_sync does not corrupt the state machine.

    Scenario: sync manager is SYNCING (awaiting set_usercode). While waiting,
    the coordinator gets a push_update with different data. The _request_sync_check
    callback fires but should be a no-op since state is SYNCING.
    """
    await async_initial_tick(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)

    lock_provider = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data.locks[LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]
    coordinator = lock_provider.coordinator
    assert coordinator is not None
    in_sync_entity_obj = get_in_sync_entity_obj(hass, SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY)
    mgr = in_sync_entity_obj._sync_manager

    # Verify starting in sync
    assert hass.states.get(SLOT_1_IN_SYNC_ENTITY).state == STATE_ON

    # Make out of sync by changing the coordinator data (external change)
    lock_provider.codes[1] = "0000"
    await coordinator.async_refresh()
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    # Change PIN so there is a mismatch to sync
    await hass.services.async_call(
        TEXT_DOMAIN,
        TEXT_SERVICE_SET_VALUE,
        service_data={ATTR_VALUE: "9999"},
        target={ATTR_ENTITY_ID: SLOT_1_PIN_ENTITY},
        blocking=True,
    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    mid_sync_event = asyncio.Event()
    resume_event = asyncio.Event()
    original_set = lock_provider.async_set_usercode

    async def set_usercode_with_pause(code_slot, usercode, name=None, **kwargs):
        """Set usercode but pause mid-operation so the test can push an update."""
        mid_sync_event.set()
        await resume_event.wait()
        return await original_set(code_slot, usercode, name, **kwargs)

    with patch.object(lock_provider, "async_set_usercode", set_usercode_with_pause):
        # Force to OUT_OF_SYNC so tick will attempt sync
        mgr._state = SyncState.OUT_OF_SYNC

        # Start the tick as a background task
        tick_task = hass.async_create_task(mgr._async_tick())
        # Wait deterministically until the mock signals it has been entered
        await asyncio.wait_for(mid_sync_event.wait(), timeout=5)

        # At this point state should be SYNCING
        assert mgr._state is SyncState.SYNCING

        # Push a different code -- this fires _request_sync_check, which
        # should be a no-op because we are in SYNCING state
        coordinator.push_update({1: SlotCredential.known("7777")})

        # State should still be SYNCING (push did not corrupt it)
        assert mgr._state is SyncState.SYNCING

        # Let the set_usercode complete
        resume_event.set()
        await tick_task
        await hass.async_block_till_done()

fix: the coordinator owns a write from sent to seen

An active slot the lock verifiably reports empty is never in sync. Before,
calculate_in_sync trusted our own last write over the lock's word, so a
credential deleted out from under us kept reporting synchronized (#1538).

Fixing that alone leaves polled locks re-syncing every tick until their scan
interval catches up, so a confirmed write now stays pending until a read or
push shows it on the lock. That bookkeeping moves off the provider and the
sync tick and onto the coordinator, which already owned the reads:

- record_write / pending_write / drop_pending / observe_push / take_failed_write
  replace the provider's _pending_writes dict, the coordinator's _unverified
  flag and mark_verified. is_verified is exactly "nothing pending here".
- One confirmation look per lock: a non-eager task straight after the write,
  then a timer every CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL while anything is pending. Pollers
  are read through their poll path scoped to managed and pending slots; push
  providers hard-refresh. A failed read charges no breaker and keeps waiting;
  past PENDING_WRITE_TTL it gives the write up.
- A write fails when a read past the deadline still does not show it, or
  when a read shows the slot holding a different code. The tick takes that
  as one slot-breaker charge and re-syncs on the next tick, so a confirming
  push landing in between still counts first.
- The tick no longer reads: with a write pending it parks in
  PENDING_CONFIRMATION; a stale pending write (desired changed) is dropped
  without a charge.
- zwave_js pushes the value it wrote before returning CONFIRMED, like every
  other push provider; the seam records nothing pending for a push provider
  on that strength.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## Proposed change

One of the four symptoms in #1538: LCM reported users as **in sync** while `matter.get_lock_users` showed the lock held no PIN credentials at all.

### The bug

`calculate_in_sync` overrode a lock that said the slot held nothing, on the strength of the last PIN it wrote there. Nothing made that write *recent*: `_last_set_pin` was set on every successful write and cleared only by a clear or a restart. A poll that read the slot empty marked the address verified, the override passed, and a credential deleted out of band read as synchronized forever, with no tick to put it back because a slot in sync has nothing to do.

### The fix

An active slot the lock verifiably reports empty is never in sync. Full stop, no clock.

That alone would make a polled lock re-sync every tick until its scan interval caught up with its own write, so a **confirmed write stays pending until a read or push has seen it on the lock**. #1539 built that on the provider and the sync tick and never converged: four review rounds each found a new hole in the same place, because the tick and the coordinator were two schedulers over one piece of state (a read the tick asked for that the coordinator throttled; a throttle keyed on the wrong read; a timeout that could charge without a read; a read failure charging the lock breaker at tick cadence). This PR gives the whole thing to the coordinator, which already owned the reads.

**The coordinator owns a write from sent to seen.**

- `record_write(address, pin, believed=)` is the seam's one call after a write. OPTIMISTIC is recorded *believed* (the value shows at once); a poller's CONFIRMED is recorded *not believed* (the cloud accepted it, the lock has not said); a push provider's CONFIRMED records nothing, because its own push is the lock's word. `is_verified(address)` is exactly "nothing pending here". The `_unverified` set, `mark_verified`, and the provider's `_pending_writes` dict are gone.
- **One confirmation look per lock**, however many slots are pending: a task straight after the write (non-eager, so it cannot reenter the provider before the provider's own write has returned), then a timer every `CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL` (a quarter of `PENDING_WRITE_TTL`) while anything is pending. Pollers are read through their poll path, scoped to managed and pending slots so a direct write to an unmanaged slot is asked about too; push providers hard-refresh. The look never charges the lock breaker: a failed read is not the lock's word.
- **A write fails** when a read past the deadline still does not show it, or when a read (or push) shows the slot holding a *different* code. Both are the lock not keeping what we wrote, and both leave one charge for the tick to take via `take_failed_write`, once. A read that keeps failing past the deadline gives the write up too, so a lock whose writes land but whose reads never return still ends in a visible re-sync and suspend, not a silent pending state.
- **The tick only watches.** With a write pending it parks in `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` and issues no read of its own; a pending write the user no longer wants (PIN changed, slot disabled) is dropped without a charge; a failed write is charged and re-synced on the *next* tick, so a confirming push landing in between still counts first. The post-set refresh is skipped when the coordinator has already gone to read the lock back.
- **zwave_js pushes the value it wrote before returning CONFIRMED**, like every other push provider. It was the one that did not, which left a stale `empty()` on the coordinator to be judged against.

### What it does not carry from #1539

- `_last_set_pin` stays on the sync manager. Moving it to the provider is right (direct writes bypass the sync manager) but is its own change, and Matter's `async_release_managed_slot` would need to forget it too.
- The pre-existing AVAILABLE guard in zwave_js has the same deletion-hiding shape as the guard reverted in #1539, and the three "expects a PIN" guards across zwave_js/zwave_js_ui should be one predicate or none. Both noted, neither touched here.

### Verification

- Full suite green at 100% line coverage under HA 2026.9.0b4.
- Sixteen mutants, one per invariant, each killed by the test written for it: verified-empty active slot never in sync; unverified slot never in sync; poller CONFIRMED pending until seen; push CONFIRMED records nothing; zwave_js pushes before returning; absent read before the deadline keeps waiting; absent read at the deadline fails the write once; displaced readable read fails the write (read and push paths); one look per lock; the look does not start eagerly; a stale drop does not charge; the tick charges a failed write; the tick does not read while a write is pending.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: the false in-sync symptom of #1538 (the other three symptoms are tracked there and are not closed by this PR)
- This PR is related to issue: #1538
- Supersedes #1539, which is closed in favour of this redesign.

  holding a *different* readable code is not just "external change wins": it

  verification miss and charged the breaker; without it a controller fighting
  over a slot re-sets forever without ever suspending. So `_expired` became

  assertions moved from `push_update({slot: value})` to

  on the coordinator.

  timer lingers and phacc fails the test at teardown.

For providers where the underlying integration's value cache updates asynchronously (e.g., Z-Wave JS
push notifications), implement optimistic updates to prevent sync loops:

```python
async def async_set_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef, value: str, ...) -> WriteResult:
    # ... perform the set operation ...
    await self._call_service_to_set_code(ref.slot, value)

    # Optimistic update: the command succeeded, so tell the coordinator now
    # rather than waiting for a cache that updates later.
    self._push_credential_update(
        ref.slot, SlotCredential.known(value), optimistic=True
    )
    return WriteResult(changed=True)

async def async_delete_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef) -> bool:
    # ... perform the clear operation ...
    await self._call_service_to_clear_code(ref.slot)

    self._push_credential_update(ref.slot, SlotCredential.empty(), optimistic=True)
    return True

<result>## Error-handling review: PR #1545 (`fix/1538-coordinator-owns-pending`)

Worktree: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/pending-b`. All line numbers below are from the branch's working tree.

### 1. HIGH — A read that *fails* past the deadline is counted as the lock *declining* the write, the charge survives an outage, and the only record of why is at DEBUG

`custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/coordinator.py:437-451`:
```python
except LockCodeManagerError as err:
    _LOGGER.debug("Confirmation read failed for %s: %s", ...)
    self._expire_overdue()
    return
```
and `_expire_overdue` (`:457-463`) does `self._failed_writes.add(address)` — the same bucket a read that *observed* the slot absent/displaced uses. `_failed_writes` is cleared only by `record_write` (`:285`), `drop_pending` (`:311`) and `take_failed_write` (`:325`); nothing on lock recovery touches it.

`custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/sync.py:786-789` gates on `self._coordinator.unreachable` *before* `take_failed_write` at `:815-824`, which logs `"%s: write not confirmed within the timeout; re-syncing (attempt %s)"` and charges the slot breaker.

Scenario: set accepted; lock drops offline 5 s later. Four confirmation reads raise `LockDisconnected` (four DEBUG lines). At 60 s `_expire_overdue` marks the write failed. Poll failures trip the lock breaker, tick returns SUSPENDED (unreachable) — flag kept. Lock recovers, `_reset_backoff` runs, next tick: `take_failed_write` is True, the slot breaker takes a charge and the WARNING says the write was not confirmed. Nothing at INFO or above ever said the lock was unreadable for the whole TTL, so a user debugging a later suspension sees "write not confirmed" ×3 with no hint it was an outage. On a push lock there is no scheduled poll, so `unreachable` is never even set by the read failures and the charge lands at TTL immediately. The docstring's claim "connectivity is the scheduled poll's to judge" (`:421-422`) does not hold for push providers.

Fix (one line each): in both except branches, drop overdue writes instead of failing them when the read itself failed (`self._pending` pop only), or at minimum log the give-up at WARNING including `err` so the later tick warning has a cause on record; and clear `_failed_writes` in `_reset_backoff`.

### 2. HIGH — `drop_pending` runs *before* the clear executes, so a failed clear leaves a believed, unconfirmed PIN in `data` marked verified

`custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py:1485-1491`:
```python
if self.coordinator is not None:
    self.coordinator.drop_pending(pin_address(code_slot))
changed = await self._execute_rate_limited("clear", ...)
```
`record_write(believed=True)` pushed `SlotCredential.known(pin)` into `data` (`coordinator.py:286-289`); `drop_pending` pops only `_pending`/`_failed_writes` (`:310-311`) and never reverts `data`; `is_verified` is `not in self._pending` (`:253`).

Scenario: zwave_js returns `OPTIMISTIC` (`zwave_js.py:677`) → `data[slot] = known("1234")`, pending. User calls the direct clear service; `_execute_bounded` raises `LockDisconnected` at the availability check (`_base.py:344-352`) before any device traffic. Now: no pending, `data` still says `known("1234")`, slot config still ON. Next tick: `calculate_in_sync` → `credential.matches("1234")` (`sync.py:481`) → IN_SYNC, breaker reset. The confirmation machinery is bypassed; the write is never read back. On `main`, `_pending_writes.pop` did not discard from `_unverified`, so the slot stayed unverified — this is a regression.

Fix: move `drop_pending` to after `_execute_rate_limited` returns (a clear that raised superseded nothing), or have `drop_pending` revert a `believed` write's value in `data`.

### 3. MEDIUM — Post-read processing sits outside the try; a raise there strands pending writes with neither task nor timer

`coordinator.py:452`: `new_data = {**self.data, **self._apply_read(self._normalize_keys(raw))}` is after the `try/except`. `_normalize_keys` raises `ValueError/TypeError` on a non-int key (`:200`). In `_async_confirmation_look` (`:358-366`) the `finally` clears `_confirm_task` but the `if self._pending:` re-arm is skipped on exception; same in `_async_confirmation_timer` (`:368-374`). The tick then holds PENDING_CONFIRMATION (`sync.py:797-804`) and never reads on its own. HA's task handler logs the traceback, so it is not silent, but the write sits until the 1-min scheduled poll (polled) or the drift check (push) runs `_apply_read` (`coordinator.py:638`, `:658`) — and the same bad key makes those raise too. Cancellation is handled correctly: `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, propagates past the re-arm, no timer is armed after shutdown.

Fix: pull the `_normalize_keys`/`_apply_read`/merge lines inside the `try` so the existing `except Exception` (which already calls `_expire_overdue`) covers them.

### 4. MEDIUM — Once the timer has fired, neither handle tracks it; shutdown cannot cancel it and it re-arms afterwards

`_async_confirmation_timer` sets `self._confirm_unsub = None` first (`:370`), and `_confirm_task` is not set for it. `async_shutdown` (`:697-702`) cancels/unsubs only those two and does not clear `_pending`. Scenario: timer fires, read in flight, entry unloads → shutdown is a no-op → read completes (or raises `LockDisconnected`, DEBUG) → `if self._pending:` re-arms `async_call_later` on a torn-down coordinator; repeats up to 4 more reads against the unloaded provider until `_expire_overdue` drains at TTL. Bounded and quiet, but it is provider traffic after unload with no log above DEBUG.

Fix: `self._pending.clear()` in `async_shutdown`, and gate the re-arm on a shutdown flag (or run the timer body as `_confirm_task`).

### 5. LOW — Same failure, two log levels; a `ProviderNotImplementedError` would be swallowed at DEBUG forever

`async_internal_hard_refresh_codes` failing is WARNING in `_async_drift_check` (`coordinator.py:668-672`) but DEBUG in the confirmation path (`:437-443`). `ProviderNotImplementedError` is a `LockCodeManagerError` (`domain/exceptions.py:116`), so a push provider without `async_hard_refresh_codes` would have every `OPTIMISTIC` write expire as failed with only DEBUG output. Latent today: only zwave_js emits `OPTIMISTIC` and it implements hard refresh (`zwave_js.py:1137`). Fix: log the confirmation-read failure at INFO with `err`, matching the "expected condition is info" rule.

### Questions with no finding

- **Q1 (what is caught):** `LockCodeManagerError` → DEBUG; `Exception` → `_LOGGER.exception` (ERROR + traceback). `_expire_overdue()` runs on both (`:443`, `:450`). `CancelledError` is not caught. The broad except is justified — it is what keeps the look/timer chain alive — and ERROR is the right level for a programming error. The `asyncio.timeout` wrapper converts a hung read to `LockDisconnected` (`_base.py:311-331`), so hangs land in the specific branch. Only the placement gap in finding 3 and the level/attribution issues in findings 1 and 5.
- **Q4 (seam branches):** No gap. `NO_CHANGE` → early return with nothing recorded (`_base.py:1358-1359`), and the tick's `else` branch still refreshes polled locks (`sync.py:957-960`) and judges push locks via `calculate_in_sync` + `was_set` charge (`:990`) — visible, same as `main`. Only `virtual.py:137` returns `NO_CHANGE`. An exception after the lock accepted the write records nothing, which is consistent with `_last_set_pin` (set only after the await, `sync.py:519`) and with `_cleared_slots.discard` deliberately happening before (`_base.py:1327`); the tick's except handlers set OUT_OF_SYNC and the retry is verified by refresh.
- **Q5 (`slots` plumbing):** `async_internal_get_usercodes` passes `slots` only when given (`_base.py:2062-2075`). Only zwave_js overrides `async_get_usercodes` and it accepts `slots` (`zwave_js.py:323-325`). Every provider's `async_get_users` accepts `slots` (akuvox:307, virtual:153, schlage:301, zha:358, matter:457, zwave_js:262, zwave_js_ui:1223, zigbee2mqtt:581). `_project_users_to_slots` seeds every requested slot with `empty()` (`_base.py:1540-1541`), so a pending address is always present in the read and `_apply_read` can settle or expire it. No `TypeError` path.

Ordering of severity is mine; finding 1 touches a stated design choice ("gives that write up all the same"), so the parent may prefer the logging-only fix over changing what `_expire_overdue` does on a failed read.</result>

Mutant B (flag survives `record_write`) survived. `coordinator.py:285` is the only guard. Scenario: a read past the TTL fails the write; before the tick runs, a direct `set_usercode` service call re-records the address (the tick's pending block at `domain/sync.py` runs before `take_failed_write`, so the flag is never consumed); the read confirms; the next tick charges the breaker for a write the lock kept. Suggested: record, expire via `_apply_read` past the deadline, record again, confirm via a present `_apply_read`, assert `take_failed_write` is False.

**3. `record_write` replacing an existing pending PIN is unproven (rating 7)**

Bug missed: two quick PIN changes leave the older PIN pending; the read shows the newer code as a "readable different code", counts the write failed, and charges the breaker. Suggested: a parametrized contract test over the push providers asserting `coordinator.data[slot]` is present after a CONFIRMED set, or a `MockLCMPushLock`-backed tick test.

2026-09-02 — Decision: Option B, "the coordinator owns a write from sent to seen" (Raman: "lets go with Option B"), shipped as lock_code_manager PR #1545 (branch fix/1538-coordinator-owns-pending), superseding PR #1539.

Why: PR #1539 kept the core fix (an active slot the lock verifiably reports empty is never in sync — the #1538 false in-sync) but its confirmation machinery failed four review rounds in the same place, because the sync tick and the coordinator were two schedulers over one piece of pending-write state.

Design as implemented:
- record_write(address, pin, believed=) is the seam's one call after a write. OPTIMISTIC → believed (value shown at once). Poller CONFIRMED → not believed (cloud accepted, lock has not said). Push-provider CONFIRMED → nothing recorded (its own push is the lock's word; drop_pending supersedes older). is_verified(address) == address not in _pending. _unverified, mark_verified, provider _pending_writes deleted.
- One confirmation look per lock: non-eager task straight after the write (hass.async_create_task(..., eager_start=False) — eager reentered the provider from inside its own write path; async_call_later(0) never fires under async_block_till_done), then async_call_later every CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL = PENDING_WRITE_TTL/4 = 15 s while anything is pending. Pollers read via async_internal_get_usercodes(managed ∪ pending); push providers hard-refresh. The look never charges the lock breaker.
- A write FAILS when a read past the deadline still does not show it, or when a read/push shows the slot holding a different readable code (displaced write; without this a controller fighting over a slot re-sets forever). Both set _failed_writes; take_failed_write hands the tick exactly one slot-breaker charge; re-sync happens on the NEXT tick so a confirming push in between counts first.

## Review round 1 on PR #1545 (2026-09-02)

Three reviewers (correctness tracer, silent-failure hunter, test-quality
analyzer). No HIGH from the tracer: breaker arithmetic, restart, tick PENDING
handling, observe/push split all clean. Fixed in round 1:

- **Clear ordering (regression, HIGH):** `drop_pending` ran before the clear
  executed; a believed optimistic write + a clear raising at the availability
  check left `known(pin)` in data, unpending → verified → falsely in sync.
  Now dropped only after the clear ran.
- **Timer read untracked:** the timer callback awaited the read directly, so
  both `_confirm_task` and `_confirm_unsub` were None during it → a
  `record_write` in that window started a second chain, and shutdown could not
  cancel it. Now `_start_look()` is the single entry (record_write and timer);
  the timer read is the tracked task. `async_shutdown` clears `_pending` and
  `_failed_writes`.
- **Merge outside try:** `_normalize_keys`/`_apply_read` moved inside so a
  provider bug cannot strand the chain.
- **Replace, don't merge:** the scoped read has poll shape (managed ∪ pending
  plus occupied unmanaged), so the confirmation read replaces data like the
  poll and drift paths; an unmanaged code deleted out of band now disappears.
- **Failed write that leaves the slot in sync:** a direct write of X the lock
  did not keep (slot still holds configured P) set `_failed_writes` with no
  data change → no listener → flag lingered until an unrelated later sync was
  charged. Now the coordinator calls `async_update_listeners()` when a write
  fails without moving the data (read, push, and give-up paths) and
  `request_sync_check` discards the flag when the slot is still in sync.
- **Give-up logging:** failed read past the deadline logs INFO with the cause
  and slots; a failure that leaves everything waiting stays DEBUG.

Kept as design: a read that keeps failing past the deadline FAILS the write
(dropping it would trust a believed value the lock never confirmed — the
#1538 shape). Known limit, not this PR: zwave_js_ui API-only maps a timed-out
slot read to `unreadable`, which confirms a pending write (pre-existing; the
credential-state model question).

Tests added: observe_push with nothing pending; newer record_write replaces
the pending PIN; record_write clears an earlier failed flag; no duplicate
look while the timer is armed / during a timer read; shutdown with an armed
timer and with a timer read in flight; unusable read key does not strand the
look; deleted unmanaged slot vanishes; push-provider seam contract on a real
coordinator; external deletion via push drives the tick to re-program (#1538
class); failed direct write on an in-sync slot discarded (read and push).
8 round-1 mutants all killed.
EOF

## Findings

### 1. MEDIUM — a pending address the read never names is never settled; on a push lock that is a hard refresh every 15s for the life of the coordinator

`/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/pending-b/custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/coordinator.py:225` (`_apply_read`) only visits `observed.items()`; `_give_up_overdue` (`:467`) only runs when the read *raises*. A pending address that a *successful* read does not mention is untouched, and `_async_confirmation_look:372` re-arms the timer because `_pending` is non-empty:

```python
for address, cred in observed.items():
    pending = self._pending.get(address)
```

For polled locks the look scopes the read to `managed_slots | pending` (`:441-443`) so every pending slot is named. For push locks it calls `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()` (`:439`), which has no scope: zwave_js's `async_hard_refresh_codes` (`providers/zwave_js.py:1146`) returns `async_get_usercodes()` = managed scope plus whatever the lock holds. A pending slot that is not managed and that the lock does not hold is absent from every read.

Scenarios: (a) a direct service write to an unmanaged slot on a masked zwave_js lock returns OPTIMISTIC (`_base.py:1366`) and never lands; (b) a managed slot is removed from the entry while its write is pending on a push lock; (c) a bridged lock flips to push via `note_push_capability` mid-pending. Reproduced with a scratch test (`/tmp/lcm_review/test_scratch_pending_absent.py`, run with `PYTHONPATH=. /tmp/ha29/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/lcm_review/... --rootdir=. -c pyproject.toml -q --no-cov -p no:randomly`): after 105s of monotonic time, 8 hard refreshes, `_pending` still holds the write, `take_failed_write` is False, timer still armed. For zwave_js that is `get_users` + `get_all_credentials` on a battery lock every 15s until restart. No wrong sync state (no manager for the slot), hence MEDIUM.

Fix: in `async_confirm_pending_writes`, after `_apply_read`, give up every pending address that is `not in raw` and past its deadline (the same sweep `_give_up_overdue` does, keyed on absence from the read rather than on read failure).

### 2. MEDIUM at HEAD (closed by the uncommitted working-tree edit) — `record_write` after `async_shutdown` starts a look against a torn-down provider

`coordinator.py:263-290` has no shutdown guard; `_start_look:360` creates a task. `__init__.py:1152-1159` calls `lock.async_unload(...)` then `coordinator.async_shutdown()`, and sync managers are stopped first (`:1209-1222`), so the sync path cannot hit this — but a direct service write awaiting the provider during unload returns afterwards, records, and the look runs `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes` / `async_internal_get_usercodes` on the unloaded lock, re-arming every 15s until the deadline sweep (~75s). The on-disk `if self._shutdown_requested: return` in `record_write` is the right fix; `_shutdown_requested` is set by HA's `DataUpdateCoordinator.async_shutdown` (`update_coordinator.py:212`). Commit it.

`const.py:208-212` says three TTLs fitting in `SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW` guarantees the trip. But nothing outside a completed read enforces the deadline (the tick "only watches", `sync.py:796-818`), so one failed-write cycle is TTL + up to `CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL` + read R + rate-limit + set W + two ticks: give-up lands at ≤ 75s + R, cycle ≈ 81 + R + W. Three failures span two cycles; `CircuitBreaker.tripped` (`resilience.py`) needs the third within 300s of the first, so it trips iff R + W ≲ 69s. Single slot: fine. N slots re-syncing serially behind `_aio_lock` (`_base.py:353-380`, 2s minimum each) push W to N×(2+W_op): ten slots at 5s each = 70s and the breaker never trips — every slot rewrites forever at ~2.5 min cadence. A look parked behind `_aio_lock` up to `OPERATION_TIMEOUT` (600s) stretches one cycle past the whole window on its own. The pre-PR tick charged at TTL regardless of reads; the PR deliberately removed that, so this is a trade to confirm, not an oversight. Fix options: have the tick's pending block give up on `now >= pending.deadline` when the look has not completed, or shrink TTL/interval and correct the comment to state the real bound.

### 4. LOW — an outage after an accepted write is still charged as a declined write

`sync.py:783-794` orders the unreachable check ahead of the pending block "so an outage right after an accepted write reads as the outage it is". But `_give_up_overdue` (`coordinator.py:467-493`) marks the write failed after 60s of `LockDisconnected`, and on recovery `SUSPENDED -> OUT_OF_SYNC -> take_failed_write` charges a strike and warns "write not confirmed within the timeout" (`sync.py:824-833`). One strike (the breaker was just reset on resume), then re-sync; deliberate per the PR text, but it contradicts the tick comment. Fix: skip the give-up (or record it as outage, not failure) when the error is `LockDisconnected` / `_lock_breaker.tripped`.

### 5. LOW — banked failures with no one to take them

`_failed_writes` entries survive until some tick calls `take_failed_write`. Unmanaged-slot direct writes never get one; a manager in SUSPENDED-with-target, or IN_SYNC with `snapshot is None` (`sync.py:643-653`), does not discard. If the slot later becomes managed, the first OUT_OF_SYNC tick charges and warns for a write made long ago. At HEAD `async_confirm_pending_writes:461` (`elif self._failed_writes:`) also wakes every listener on every no-change look while any stale entry exists; the on-disk `failed_before` narrows the wake but not the banking. `_start_look:355` returns when `_confirm_unsub` is set, so the "task straight after the write" only holds for the first pending slot on a lock; a later slot sits in PENDING_CONFIRMATION up to `CONFIRM_READ_INTERVAL` longer. `test_record_write_while_the_timer_is_armed_starts_no_second_look` pins this as intended. Work on Option B is complete and PR #1545 is ready for your review.

**What shipped.** PR #1545, "fix: the coordinator owns a write from sent to seen (#1538)", seven commits on `fix/1538-coordinator-owns-pending`, replacing #1539 (closed with a supersession note). The coordinator now owns every pending write: the seam records it, one confirmation look per lock reads it back (a non-eager task right after the write, then a timer every quarter-TTL), a write fails when a read past the deadline still does not show it or shows a different code, and the tick only watches and takes one charge per failed write. An active slot the lock verifiably reports empty is never in sync.

**Verification.**
- Full suite green at 100% line coverage under HA 2026.9.0b4; every hook passes; CI green on every push so far, with the pytest job still running on the final test-only commit.
- 37 mutants across three rounds, each killed by the test written for it.

**Review history.** Three rounds, as you asked, plus verifiers.
- Round one found a real regression (the clear dropped a pending write before it ran) and three lifecycle edges: an untracked timer read, a merge outside the try, and a failed write that moved no data never waking listeners. All fixed.
- Round two found nothing HIGH. Its one MEDIUM was a completed read that never names a pending slot, which left a push lock hard-refreshing every 15 s for good. Fixed by judging an unnamed slot like an absent one.
- Round three found nothing in the design. Its one conditional MEDIUM was a pre-existing zwave_js mapping (an empty code event taken as "cleared" without the occupancy check) that the fix made consequential. Fixed with the read path's own rule, and the driver's status-then-code ordering is now pinned by a test.

**Two things I decided rather than asked, flagged for you.**
- A read that keeps failing past the deadline still fails the write, costing one strike after an outage. Dropping it instead would trust a believed value the lock never confirmed, which is the #1538 shape again. Documented in the PR body.
- The breaker-trip bound is now stated honestly in the constants: one failed cycle is the TTL plus up to the read interval plus the read and the re-set, three inside the five-minute window. Scheduling is unchanged; the old bound had the same shape.

**Follow-ups, not in this PR.** The `_last_set_pin` move to the provider; zwave-js-ui API-only mode confirming a write by a timed-out read; the pre-existing zwave_js AVAILABLE guard; a comment on issue #1538 once you're happy with the PR. The second (the warning said "timeout" even for a write displaced by a different code) was fair; reworded in `da5e0634` and replied. Codecov reports every changed line covered. The full suite is green at 100% on the final commit, and CI has passed on every push so far, with the last pytest job still running.

**Have the reviews settled? Yes.** Three rounds plus verifiers, with findings converging to zero in the design:

- Round one found a real regression and three lifecycle edges, all in how the coordinator's new machinery was wired, not in the idea.
- Round two found nothing HIGH and one MEDIUM: a case I had not enumerated (a read that never *names* a pending slot), not a flaw in the ownership model.
- Round three found nothing in the design at all. Its one conditional MEDIUM was a pre-existing zwave_js mapping that the fix made consequential. Every reviewer's list of dropped hypotheses read like the design's property list: no in-sync on an unseen value, no double charge, no orphaned pending write, no re-entrancy.

**Is it the right design? I think so, for one structural reason.** #1539 failed four rounds because the sync tick and the coordinator were two schedulers acting on one piece of state; each fix moved the seam and opened a new hole. Here the state has one owner, and that owner is the component that already did the reads. The tick has no I/O and asks three questions: is a write pending, did one fail, is the slot in sync. That is why round three was clean where #1539's round four was not. The trades I made deliberately are documented in the PR body: a read that keeps failing past the deadline still fails the write (the alternative trusts an unconfirmed value, which is the #1538 shape again), and the breaker bound is now stated as the real sum rather than "three TTLs". Two residual smells worth your eye, neither blocking: the failed-write flag is a small second channel between coordinator and tick (banked by one, consumed by the other), and `_last_set_pin` still lives on the sync manager, which is the follow-up already noted.

**Does it address #1538? Partly, and honestly only one of the four symptoms directly.** It fixes the false in-sync: users reporting "in sync" while the lock held no PIN credentials. Because that bug hid out-of-band deletions, the fix also changes what the other symptoms look like: a credential that disappears from the lock now shows as out of sync and is re-synced, instead of silently staying gone. The cause of the cross-lock deletion is still not found (four theories disproven by reproduction; it needs the reporter's debug logs), the wrong-attribution symptom is reframed as a PIN/slot mispairing at write time and not touched here, and the degenerate `lcm3/4/5` names are cosmetic and self-healing. The PR body says so, and links #1538 as related rather than closing it. Once you're happy with the PR, a comment on #1538 explaining which symptom it fixes and asking for debug logs on the deletion is the next step.

You were right that LCM was trusting its own state rather than verifying the credential. ### 4. `lcm3` / `lcm4` / `lcm5` — root cause found, fix in progress

Confirmed. LCM writes the Matter `userName` as `lcm:<slot>:<name>`, with fallbacks to `lcm<slot>` and then `<slot>` for firmware that rejects the colons. The bug is that it falls back on **any** error from the lock — including a transient one. Your logs show repeated poll failures, so a lock that was merely busy for a moment cost those slots their display name permanently, on a lock that demonstrably accepts colons (slots 1 and 2 prove it).

Worth stressing: `lcm3` still identifies the slot correctly. Nothing is mis-bound — only the display name was lost.

### 9 / 3. Attribution — this is a write bug, not an event bug

Your hypothesis #9 asks whether LCM mishandles a reported credential index that differs from its user index. I traced it, and the resolver is not where this goes wrong. Every name in your table decodes to the correct slot:

```
'lcm:1:User A' -> slot 1      'lcm3' -> slot 3
'lcm:2:User B' -> slot 2      'lcm4' -> slot 4
```

The slot bindings on the lock are intact, and the event resolver would map them correctly by either route it uses (`userIndex`, or the `credentialIndex` walk). So when User D's PIN produced a slot-3 event, the lock genuinely matched that PIN against **slot 3's stored credential**. Together with User C's PIN not opening the door at all, that points at a PIN landing against the wrong user at write time — your hypothesis **#7**, not #9.

The user_index ordering you saw (LCM slot 1 landing at Matter index 5) is benign, by the way — that is a failed first attempt for slot 1 being rolled back, freeing index 1 for slot 2, with slot 1 retrying into 5 later.

### 1. Cross-lock deletion — not reproduced, and I could use your logs

This is the one I have least to offer on, so rather than speculate, here is what I ruled out. I drove the real configuration paths with two locks and five users and watched every call:

- The removal diff is correct — removing lock B releases only lock B's slots. Lock A was told to release nothing.
- The options flow does not renumber anyone; existing users keep their slot numbers by design.
- The Matter provider resolves its node per device, so it cannot address the wrong lock.
- The only two code paths in the integration that can automatically delete a Matter user are the removal loop and a rollback of a just-created user. Neither can target a lock that stayed in the configuration.

Given you were also deleting users through **Manage access** during this period, one real possibility is that Lock A was emptied by something other than the removal, and the false in-sync above is what made it look causal — by guaranteeing nothing ever repaired it.

To get further I would need `lock_code_manager` debug logs covering the removal:

```yaml
logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.lock_code_manager: debug
```

The lines that would settle it name the lock and slot directly, e.g. `no LCM-owned user to release for slot N` or `Setting usercode on lock.<entity> slot N`. If those name Lock A during a removal of Lock B, that is the smoking gun and I will have it immediately.

### On your workaround

Your advice stands, and I would keep following it until #1539 ships: verify with `matter.get_lock_users` rather than the in-sync sensors, and hold off on using `code_slot_name` for security-sensitive attribution. Both cautions are well founded.

==============================================================================
#1528 [OPEN] Operation deadline scales with managed_slots, not the operation's actual scope
by raman325 2026-08-30T21:24:30Z labels=['bug'] comments=0
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`operation_timeout_seconds` scales the per-slot budget by `len(self.managed_slots)` (`zha.py`, `_mqtt.py`), which is not what any individual operation walks. Under-budget for a wide read on an entry that manages little (allocation's throwaway provider manages nothing, so a bulk-add occupancy scan gets the flat floor and can fail the read that gates adding users); over-budget for a one-slot write on a large entry.

Reachability is narrow — roughly ≥7 indices on a flaky ZHA lock or ≥60 on zigbee2mqtt — and the failure is `occupancy_unknown`, which refuses to issue a number rather than issuing one over an unchecked credential. Safe direction, and retryable.

## The real fix, and why the attempt in #1529 was abandoned

The root is that the deadline sits **outside a loop**. `async_get_users` on ZHA and both MQTT bridges walks the slots one command at a time, so a budget around the whole call must cover every trip in it — which is what forces it to scale, makes the count unknowable from the call site, and makes it unknowable entirely for a throwaway provider. Bounding **per exchange** dissolves all of that and detects a silent lock in ~90s instead of after the whole walk.

#1529 tried it and was closed unmerged. It works, but three constraints have to be respected and were not:

1. **Some providers already bound their own exchanges.** `zigbee2mqtt.py:648` wraps its read in `asyncio.wait_for(..., 10.0)` and `_per_slot_read_budget` is also `10.0`. An outer wrapper at the same figure starts earlier and always wins, converting one silent slot into a whole-poll `LockDisconnected` — which bypasses `_async_read_slots`' one-silent-slot-is-routine guard, its two-slot minimum, and the `_reads_have_succeeded` latch that exist for #1397-class lossy meshes. Wrap only where there is no inner bound.
2. **`except TimeoutError` cannot tell whose deadline fired.** zigpy's `Device.request` raises `TimeoutError` itself after its retry ladder, so catching it converts a single flaky slot into a failed walk instead of an unreadable slot. Use `async with asyncio.timeout(...) as cm:` and check `cm.expired()`.
3. **The outer deadline must not also wrap a self-bounding walk.** Once the per-slot overrides are deleted the outer budget is flat 600s, and nine ZHA slots answering in ~70s each is 630s — a false `LockDisconnected` on a lock that answered every command, which is what `OPERATION_TIMEOUT`'s own comment says must never happen. The backstop needs to apply only to calls that do not bound their own exchanges.

Doing this well probably means a provider stating whether it self-bounds, rather than a number anyone has to scale.

## Additional information

- Related: #1523, #1525, #1526, #1527, #1535, #1536
- `main` already carries the working core: a deadline on the provider call raising `LockDisconnected` (#1525), the setup retry re-arm (#1526), and deadlines on the availability probes and provider setup (#1527). This issue is the remaining refinement, not the fix itself.

==============================================================================
#1535 [OPEN] The queue on _aio_lock is unbounded even though each holder is not
by raman325 2026-09-01T04:35:51Z labels=['bug'] comments=0
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Found reviewing #1529, and attempted there before being reverted — the naive fix is worse than the gap.

Every operation now cuts itself off at its own budget, so no single call parks forever. The *queue* has no such bound. Every slot on an entry ticks on its own `async_track_time_interval` (`sync.py:296`), they all pile onto one `_aio_lock`, and a slot already in `SYNCING` short-circuits its next tick (`sync.py:709`) rather than backing off. So N wedged slots drain in N full budgets — ten ZHA slots at 900s is 2.5 hours. Finite, unlike before #1525, but it is still the multi-hour park #1523 described.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

#1529 tried refusing a caller that had *queued* when the breaker already called the lock unreachable. Two problems, both confirmed:

1. **It throws away fresher evidence than it uses.** The availability probes run immediately above and had returned True for both layers — the lock is up — and the guard then refused with "lock is unreachable" based on a breaker flag that clears only on a successful poll.
2. **The refusal is charged back to the same breaker.** `sync.py:887` catches `LockDisconnected` and calls `note_connectivity_failure()`. So a lock that had demonstrably recovered collected one extra consecutive failure per queued slot instead of that many successful writes, driving `backoff_delay` to its 1800s ceiling. Self-reinforcing.
3. The recovery poll that `note_connectivity_failure` schedules at the moment of the trip goes through the same guard, so the probe whose entire job is noticing recovery was refused without doing any I/O.

## What it actually needs

Something that distinguishes "the lock was unreachable when I joined the queue" from "it is unreachable now", without spending device I/O to find out and without feeding its own refusals back into the breaker. Possibly a bound on the wait sized to the queue rather than to the call, or having the tick not enqueue while `unreachable`. Design work, not a guard.

## Additional information

- Related: #1523, #1525, #1529

==============================================================================
#1536 [OPEN] A bulk-add config flow can wait hours on a slow lock with nothing on screen
by raman325 2026-09-01T04:35:51Z labels=['bug'] comments=0
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Found reviewing #1529, and attempted there before being reverted — the cap chosen was below everything it bounded.

Each lock's occupancy read is bounded by that provider's budget, but `async_allocate_for` multiplies that by the width of the window and then walks locks serially with no aggregate bound. A 40-user first pass on ZHA is ~3600s per deadline. Both callers are interactive — the config flow (`config_flow.py:264`) and the `add_users` action (`services.py:513`) — so a person sits in front of a frozen dialog with no explanation.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

#1529 added a 120s `ALLOCATION_READ_TIMEOUT` over the whole of `async_allocate_for`. Every per-operation budget is floored at `OPERATION_TIMEOUT = 600.0`, so the aggregate cap fired **first, every time**, on the only path that reaches the occupancy scan. That:

- made `slot_scope=len(wanted)` — the actual fix for #1528 — inert, since the cap always bound before the scoped budget could;
- **failed locks that work on `main` today**: one needing 120–600s of honest reading now returns `occupancy_unknown`, which is the reported bug appearing on hardware that never had it.

## The real tension

A person-scale wait (~1–2 min) and a per-slot budget floored at ten minutes cannot both be satisfied by a single number. Options worth weighing:

- a *smaller per-operation* budget on the interactive path, rather than an aggregate cap over generous ones;
- a budget that scales with the users being added, so small adds stay snappy and bulk adds are allowed to take longer;
- progress feedback instead of a bound, so a long read is legible rather than silent.

This needs a decision about which of those, not another constant.

## Additional information

- Related: #1523, #1528, #1529

## Proposed change

Fixes #1528.

The deadline was outside a loop. `async_get_users` on ZHA and on both MQTT bridges walks the slots one command at a time, so a budget placed around the whole call had to cover every trip in it — and that single misplacement generated every problem this PR went through:

- the budget had to scale with the slot count, so ZHA and `BaseMqttLock` each overrode it;
- the count isn't knowable from the call site, so `slot_scope` and `_slots_in_scope` existed to pass it in;
- scaled that large it collided with waiting on `_aio_lock`, which is what two rounds of review kept re-breaking;
- and it's unknowable for the throwaway provider allocation builds — **which is #1528**.

Bounded per exchange instead, all of that goes away:

```python
result = await self._round_trip(
    cluster.get_pin_code(slot_num), _WORST_CASE_ZCL_COMMAND
)
```

`_round_trip` wraps one command and turns silence into `LockDisconnected`. ZHA passes its `_WORST_CASE_ZCL_COMMAND`, the MQTT bridges their `_per_slot_read_budget` — constants that already existed for exactly this and were being misused as multipliers. Both provider overrides are deleted, `operation_timeout_seconds` goes back to a flat property, and `slot_scope`/`_slots_in_scope` are gone.

**Detection improves rather than regressing.** A lock that has stopped answering is caught on the first silent command — about 90s on ZHA — instead of after the walk's whole budget, which was up to 2700s and scaled with how many users you had.

The outer deadline stays as a backstop for whatever sits outside the exchanges, and needs no scaling now that nothing under it loops. It also no longer covers the wait on `_aio_lock`: one number can't answer both "how long should my call take" and "how long will I queue behind someone else's", and cancelling a caller that was only queueing raises `LockDisconnected`, which charges the consecutive lock breaker and marks healthy hardware `unreachable`.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #1528
- Mutation-verified: scaling by `managed_slots` again, dropping the scan's width declaration, re-adding a narrowing to the set or clear path, or letting `_slots_in_scope` narrow again, each fails a test that names the behaviour.
- The helper started with a `max(..., 1)` floor. No mutation could kill it — the outer `max` against the flat budget already covers a zero count — so it was removed rather than left as an untestable guard that reads like a real one.
- `operation_timeout_seconds` changes from a property to a method. Internal only; providers override it, nothing outside the integration reads it.
- Full suite green at 100% coverage (2349); `prek` clean.



- The keyword is `slot_scope`, not `slots`: `async_get_usercodes` already has a `slots` parameter riding the same `**kwargs`, so the obvious call spelling would have been swallowed as the budget scope and raised `TypeError: float * frozenset`. Latent only because the one such call site uses `partial`.

result.output:
#1523 [CLOSED] [ISSUE] A hung provider write parks a slot in SYNCING forever — no timeout, no breaker, no repair issue by jeallen2
---
### What happened?

A provider write that never returns parks a slot in `SyncState.SYNCING` **permanently**. There is no timeout on the write and `_async_tick` early-returns while the state is `SYNCING`, so that slot's reconciliation loop never runs again for the life of the config entry.

The failure is completely silent:

- no exception, so the circuit breaker is never charged and the existing suspend path never engages
- no repair issue
- nothing in `system_log` at WARNING or ERROR
- nothing in the debug log — the tick returns before it logs anything
- `binary_sensor.<lock>_code_slot_<n>_in_sync` correctly flips to `off` and then just stays there

From the outside it looks exactly like "I changed the PIN and it didn't sync", with no diagnostic signal anywhere. In my case three PIN changes sat unsynced for ~7 hours across three locks before I went looking.

I expected a hung write to eventually time out, charge the breaker, and either retry or suspend the slot with a repair issue — i.e. end in a visible state, which is what the code does for every *failing* write. A *hanging* write is the one path with no exit.

### The code path

`domain/sync.py` — `_async_tick`:

```python
if self._state in (
    SyncState.IN_SYNC,
    SyncState.SYNCING,
    SyncState.SUSPENDED,
):
    return
```

4.2.4 line 644, **unchanged at 5.5.1 line 711**.

`_async_tick_impl` sets `SYNCING` and awaits with no deadline (4.2.4 line 791, 5.5.1 line 869):

```python
self._state = SyncState.SYNCING
self._write_state()
was_set = False
try:
    was_set = await self._perform_sync(slot_state)
```

`providers/_base.py` `_execute` then awaits the provider call under `_aio_lock` (4.2.4 line 273), also with no deadline:

```python
async with self._aio_lock:
    ...
    result = await func(*args, **kwargs)
```

So a provider call that never settles holds `_aio_lock` **and** pins the slot in `SYNCING`. Every later write on that lock blocks on the mutex, producing no traffic and no error.

There is no timeout construct anywhere in `sync.py` in either version — `grep -E "wait_for|asyncio.timeout|TimeoutError"` returns nothing in 4.2.4 or 5.5.1.

### Secondary effect: unload deadlocks

`async_stop` awaits the in-flight tick tasks, so a wedged slot also makes the config entry impossible to unload. Reloading the entry hung here:

```
DEBUG [custom_components.lock_code_manager] Unload: stopping 30 sync manager(s)
```

and the entry sat in `unload_in_progress` indefinitely. It only cleared with a full Home Assistant restart. That makes the natural user recovery ("reload the integration") unavailable in exactly the situation that needs it — though a reload *does* work once the underlying provider is healthy again.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a slot against a Z-Wave lock (`zwave_js`).
2. Get the Z-Wave controller into a state where a command is accepted but never settles. In my case the USB controller had hung at the hardware level — a ping issued at 13:08 did not fail until 13:21, and only then because the driver was torn down (`ping failed: driver instance destroyed (ZW0102)`). A stalled transaction queue or an unplugged/hung stick reproduces it.
3. Change the slot's PIN.

=== merged fixes ===
#1525 MERGED 2026-08-30 fix: a wedged provider call is cut off instead of parking its slot forever
#1526 MERGED 2026-08-30 fix: a wedged capability probe no longer disables the lock for good
#1527 MERGED 2026-08-30 fix: the operation deadline covers every device call, not just the last

Two Z-Wave device dumps ~11h apart:

```
=== feedback_retry_recovery_signal_must_match_failure ===

When classifying a provider error, the question is not "is this transient?" but
"can the recovery signal of the path I'm routing to actually observe this
failure clearing?" The lock circuit breaker recovers via a **read** probe. Any
*write* failure routed to it becomes an invisible infinite loop: the write keeps
failing, the read keeps succeeding and resetting the breaker, and the only
user-visible artifact is a repeating "Update failed N consecutive times"
warning. It never escalates to a repair issue and never converges.

**Why:** issue #1398. `providers/zwave_js.py` mapped every
`BaseZwaveJSServerError` to `LockDisconnected`, including node-zwave-js
`Argument_Invalid` (322) for an out-of-range credential slot — a deterministic
argument-validation error. Fixed in PR #1401 by classifying on
`FailedZWaveCommand.zwave_error_code` and adding `LockOperationUnsupported`
(subclass of `LockOperationFailed`) for "can never succeed as specified", which
suspends the lock+slot immediately with the real reason.

**How to apply:**
- `LockDisconnected` → lock breaker, recovers on a successful read. Only for
  genuine transport failures.
- `LockOperationFailed` → slot breaker, suspends after `MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS`. For
  retryable lock-side refusals.
- `LockOperationUnsupported` → immediate per-(lock, slot) suspend. For requests
  that are invalid for the device.
- `CodeRejectedError` → disables the slot entry-wide. Only when the *PIN* is the
  problem and the user can fix it by editing the PIN.
- When enumerating external error codes, list the **permanent** ones, not the
  transient ones. An unrecognized or newly added code then degrades to the
  existing retry behavior instead of wrongly suspending a slot.
